Explanation: A care booking is an agreed session between a family and a caregiver, with a defined need, time and payment arrangement.
UrbanSitter operates the care marketplace and the employer-benefit layer that helps families find, book and pay caregivers.
UrbanSitter has to turn a family care need into a booking with a suitable available caregiver.
More successful matches can create repeat use, memberships, employer-benefit usage and a denser local care network.
UrbanSitter must maintain enough available caregivers while managing safety, quality, cancellations and uneven local supply.
UrbanSitter coordinates search, messaging, bookings, memberships, credit payments and employer-funded care benefits.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Book / Pay — Families bring care needs to UrbanSitter, book caregivers and use the platform’s membership and payment tools. | → Consumer · Match / Access — UrbanSitter gives families access to caregiver profiles, search, messaging, booking and benefit-supported care tools. | ← Provider · Profile / Time — Caregivers provide profiles, rates, skills and availability that make them searchable and bookable. | → Provider · Jobs / Pay — UrbanSitter routes family demand to caregivers and supports bookings and eligible credit payments. | ← Partner · Benefit / Credits — Employers can sponsor membership and fund Care Credits that employees use inside the marketplace.

Explanation: Annual background checks, profile review, ratings, platform rules and Member Services shape who can participate and how trust is managed.
Families can discover UrbanSitter directly through its app and website or through an employer-provided care benefit.
UrbanSitter reviews profiles, supports search and booking, processes eligible payments and care credits, and handles trust and safety issues.
Core resources include the caregiver community, family demand, profiles, reviews, booking tools, payment systems and care-benefit infrastructure.
Families and care seekers use UrbanSitter to find babysitters, nannies and other household caregivers.
Families need suitable care at a specific place and time without having to build a caregiver network from scratch.
Search, reviews, profiles and booking tools can make it faster to find a caregiver who fits the family’s needs.
Care can be expensive, and families may struggle with last-minute needs, limited local availability or uncertainty about a new caregiver.
Families search, message, book and either pay the caregiver directly or use UrbanSitter credit payments where available.

Explanation: Families compare caregiver rates, location, experience, reviews, availability and skills such as infant care, driving or tutoring.
Families use the UrbanSitter app or website; employees with a corporate benefit can enroll through their employer or organization.
Families post jobs, browse profiles, interview or message caregivers, book care, pay and leave reviews.
Families bring the care need, schedule, location, preferences, budget and payment method.
Independent caregivers offer child care and other household care services through individual UrbanSitter profiles.
Caregivers want access to local families and paid care work that fits their skills and schedule.
Caregivers can set rates and availability and use the platform to find flexible jobs and repeat family relationships.
Demand can be uneven, jobs can cancel, and caregivers also need confidence that families, schedules and payments are reliable.
Caregivers accept bookings, provide the agreed care and receive payment from families through the chosen payment method.

Explanation: Caregivers must be at least 18, maintain an active membership, complete a profile and pass the required annual background check.
Approved caregivers use UrbanSitter tools to see jobs, message families, manage bookings and receive eligible credit payments.
Caregivers maintain profiles and availability, respond to jobs, communicate with families and provide the booked care.
Caregivers bring time, care experience, references, skills, local availability and the trust built through their profile and reviews.
Employers and organizations can sponsor UrbanSitter access and care subsidies for eligible employees.
Employers use the platform to give employees access to care and, in some plans, help pay for it through Care Credits.
Care benefits can help employees handle child-care and other caregiving needs that might otherwise disrupt work.
Employers need a benefit that employees can actually use while controlling subsidy cost, eligibility and program administration.
Employer benefits can include free UrbanSitter membership and Care Credits that employees apply to eligible caregiver payments.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Benefit / Credits — Employers can sponsor membership and fund Care Credits that employees use inside the marketplace.

Explanation: Benefit access depends on the employer program and whether the employee or organization member is eligible.
Employers and eligible employees use the Corporate Care program and enrollment flow to activate membership and care benefits.
Employers set benefit rules and subsidies, communicate the program and fund the care access their employees use.
Partners contribute benefit budgets, employee eligibility data and a workforce that can bring funded demand into the marketplace.
